newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai minister optimistic over 2nd half '97 exports.
newsitem.headline: Thai minister optimistic over 2nd half '97 exports.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Friday he expects sluggish Thai exports to pick up during the rest of 1997 after their disappointing performance in the first four months.

Amnuay told reporters Thailand would likely ship out more farm commodities especially rice later this year and overall exports should post higher growth during the second half of 1997 after an exceptionally weak performance in the same period a year ago.
Thai exports increased about one percent during January/ April against a 7.7 percent growth target set by the central bank for the whole of 1997.
Thai economic growth slowed to 6.7 percent in 1996 from 8.6 percent in 1995, mainly due to weak exports which contracted 0.2 percent last year against a 23.6 percent increase in 1995.
Amnuay said he would be happy with seven percent export growth this year.

He said his optimism on exports was partly based on more letters of credit (L/C) issued by major commercial banks. He said L/Cs issued by the Siam Commercial Bank Plc this month were at least 20 percent higher than a year ago.
